texts.label: Longlée to Henri IV, duplicate of a dispatch, Madrid [Dec 1589 - Feb 1590] (BNE Mss/994 ff. 67r-67v)
texts.summary: Pierre de Ségusson, sieur de Longlée, the French resident at Madrid, wrote in cipher to Henry IV early in 1590. The packet was intercepted: its copy, “Dupp. d’une despesche”, is now in the Biblioteca Nacional de España, with two other letters of Longlée that the Spaniards had deciphered by Luis Valle de la Cerda. Those two letters (3 March and 1 April 1590) were edited by Albert Mousset in 1912 from the originals at the French Foreign Office; this one was not, and no contemporary decipherment accompanies the copy. We publish the reading as far as we could take it, gaps included: 86.3% of the words, below the 95% threshold we hold ourselves to. It shows an envoy of the Duke of Mercœur at Madrid asking that Philip II declare openly against Henry IV and seize the goods of royalist Frenchmen.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 2 Nov 2026 (French, read in part): f. 67r is coherent throughout except a few segments (duplicate sent by Bayonne; no war preparations beyond the fleet of 60-80 ships; arrival on the 21st of Tornasoni, sent by the Duke of Mercoeur to ask Philip II to declare against Henri IV, ban trade with royalist Frenchmen and seize their goods and ships; Roissieu expected for Mayenne; money 'pour entretenir la guerre'); f. 67v is patchier (Duke of Sessa to Rome, Count of Olivares, no dispatch from the King since 3 November, 'la defence de l'eglise catholique'). Updated 2 Nov 2026 after a second plate of 12 doubtful signs (pre-registered rules): the fleet is to oppose the English ('aux anglois s'ils auroient quelque deseing'); f. 67v 'presse du ‹partitent›'. 481 words, 313 certain, 102 probable, 8 restored, 58 unresolved (estimated) = 86.3%, so grade B and read in part. Key K4 validated by one measurement on a held-out portion (characters 0.874 vs controls max 0.361).
